challenges.issue: The central hop 'tokens carrying the old key id fail verification' is ASSUMED, not verified. H1 and H2 are only 0.02 apart, yet the ranking must pick a fix (roll back deploy vs re-publish key). Nothing in the evidence separates the code artifact from the config value; both sit inside the same onset minute. Presenting H2 first at 0.44 overstates a distinction the data does not make.

H3 explicitly relies on an unverified canary/scoped rollout (F6/F12 return no scope field and state full service scope), so its mechanism is unsupported; but it is also the only hypothesis that naturally explains a stable ~1/3 rate, and the uniformity question that would confirm/destroy it was never measured.

The 'no external JWKS/key-store node' reasoning (F9/F17) is used to argue the key fault surfaces in-process, but the gap list admits an un-enumerated JWKS/secret publication job (outside the config API) cannot be ruled out — the same mechanism as HIST-108. This weakens the confidence that cfg-2705 alone models the key state.

evidence_requests.question: Query auth-service error_rate broken down by instance/pod AND by deployed version/revision label for the window 13:30-15:59Z. Is the ~36% elevated error rate uniform across ALL replicas, or concentrated in a subset (one pod set, one version label = dep-5710, one AZ/node pool)? Report per-instance values and the number of instances wholly at ~0.2% vs ~36%.
evidence_requests.rationale: Discriminates H1/H2 (uniform full-scope failure) from H3 (scoped rollout subset). This is a metrics query and is NOT blocked by the down identity log pipeline. If some instances are clean, H3 rises and the fix is scoped rollback/rollforward; if all are uniformly ~36%, H3 is refuted and H1/H2 remain.

evidence_requests.question: Query any auth-service token-validation metric broken down by failure reason / error code / token kid cohort if it exists (e.g. invalid_token split by kid, or a per-kid validation-success counter) for 13:30-15:59Z. Also check whether any counter reflects 'old-key/expired-key' vs 'malformed/parse-error' rejection.
evidence_requests.rationale: This is the single decisive discriminator between H2 (kid-cohort-specific failure) and H1 (parse/malformed uniform failure). If no such metric exists, say so explicitly so we can pivot to the rollback test.

evidence_requests.question: Is there any record of a JWKS/secret/key-publication event for auth-service (outside cfg-2705) in the widened 2026-04-14T00:00Z-15:59Z window — e.g. a k8s secret update, a JWKS publish job, a cert/secret rotation — and what was dep-5710's rollout scope (canary %/AZ/version) and dep-5699's? Report explicitly if such records are not modeled/available.
evidence_requests.rationale: Tests the un-ruled-out HIST-108 mechanism (a key/secret publication step the config API may not model) against cfg-2705, and confirms whether EITHER auth change was partial rather than full-scope, which bears on the unexplained ~1/3 rate (H3).

critiques.summary: The onset is rock-solid: a clean step-change between 14:00 and 14:02Z (F1,F2,F23,F27), with exactly two contiguous auth-service changes in the window (dep-5710 deploy 14:00Z; cfg-2705 key-id rotation 14:01Z) that are the ONLY changes across all services (F6,F7,F12,F13,F14,F36), api-gateway confirmed a downstream carrier (F3,F16), and infra saturation/crash/traffic excluded (F4,F28). BUT the two leading hypotheses name DIFFERENT origins with DIFFERENT fixes — H1 = dep-5710 code/parser regression (fix: roll back deploy) vs H2 = cfg-2705 signing-key rotation (fix: re-publish/stage key) — and they remain tied at 0.40. Rounds 1-2 established that EVERY decisive discriminator is a DATA-MODEL ABSENCE, not a budget failure: no per-kid or per-error-code/'invalid_token' metric exists (F19,F20,F22,T5), no per-instance/version/AZ breakdown exists (F25,T4), auth-service logs are unsearchable (F24,F29), and there is no JWKS/secret/key-publication record type to test HIST-108 (F34,F35,T6). The unexplained ~1/3 plateau under two full-scope changes (F1,F26,F30,F36) means no available series separates a parse-wide rejection (H1) from a kid-cohort rejection (H2), and H3 (partial rollout) can be neither confirmed nor excluded because the deployment/config schemas cannot represent scope. No remaining observability or dependency query can produce the separating signal; only an operational single-revert test (outside specialist tooling) would, so sending the team back for more queries would burn minutes without changing the ranking. The team should treat the fix decision as a gamble between rolling back dep-5710 and reverting/staging cfg-2705 (or a combined revert), not as an evidence-supported conclusion.

challenges.issue: Central mechanism hop ('rewritten parser rejects ~1/3 of tokens') is ASSUMED and unmeasured; a breaking parser/library change would typically fail ~100% or a shape-specific class, not a stable 1/3, and no telemetry confirms a parse-error signature.

Central mechanism hop ('a stable ~1/3 of tokens carry the old key id') is entirely unverified; no per-kid counter, no token-mint/cohort timeline, and no JWKS/secret record exists to show any key-publication step. H2 and H1 are indistinguishable from the available data.
Temporal coincidence (deploy 14:00Z vs rotation 14:01Z, F8) cannot select between H1 and H2 because both changes precede onset within the same minute.

Temporal coincidence (rotation 14:01Z vs symptom step 14:00-14:02Z) cannot select between H2 and H1 for the same reason; ordering (library first, key one minute later) is noted but not causally probative.

Partial/canary-rollout subset mechanism is structurally plausible (natural explanation of the ~1/3 plateau) but the deployment and config schemas carry NO scope/canary/revision field (F31,F32,F33,F36) and metrics expose no instance dimension (F25), so H3 can be neither confirmed nor excluded from available data.

There is a general dating/onset caveat: a 14:00Z metric bucket is missing for auth-service (F27 notes no point emitted), so onset is bracketed to 14:00-14:02Z rather than pinned to a single minute; this does not change the verdict but weakens any claim of exact-cause alignment.
